subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class per-skill user preference sidecar, and if so should the public contract be markdown sidecar, structured skill config, or no core support?
rationale: The feature is absent in source, but adding it changes public skill loading, prompt composition, snapshot invalidation, security boundaries, and docs behavior rather than fixing an already-defined bug.

options.title: Standardize markdown sidecar
options.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that loads with the selected skill at lower precedence than `SKILL.md` and participates in prompt-version, watcher, sandbox, and security behavior.

options.title: Use structured skill config
options.body: Keep preferences under `skills.entries.*.config` and require each skill or plugin to interpret them, avoiding a new markdown prompt surface at the cost of weaker natural-language convention support.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep the current model of full skill overrides, Skill Workshop proposals, memory/global context, or manual skill instructions if maintainers do not want another skill-loading surface.

recommendation.title: Standardize markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that loads with the selected skill at lower precedence than `SKILL.md` and participates in prompt-version, watcher, sandbox, and security behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The freshest feature-history and issue timeline point to steipete around grouped skill loading, docs, and skill API/product decisions.
